info.brief: Groups game objects (soldiers) into armies, places them in a built-in or customized
info.description:
Groups game objects (soldiers) into armies, places them in a built-in or customized
pattern, and moves and rotates each army as a group. Create an army with `army_create`
and a soldier for each game object with `soldier_create`, then call `soldier_move`
from each soldier's `update` and apply the position and rotation it returns.

elements.name: PATTERN
elements.brief: The army patterns `army_create` and `army_update_pattern` take. The five named
elements.description:
The army patterns `army_create` and `army_update_pattern` take. The five named
patterns place the soldiers in built-in shapes. `CUSTOMIZED` takes its rows from the
`pattern_func` passed beside it.
types: { BOTTOM_TO_TOP_SQUARE: Hash; TOP_TO_BOTTOM_SQUARE: Hash; TRIANGLE: Hash; RHOMBUS_TALL: Hash; RHOMBUS_SHORT: Hash; CUSTOMIZED: Hash; }

elements.name: army_create
elements.brief: Creates a group of game objects (an army) with the given member padding and pattern,
elements.description:
Creates a group of game objects (an army) with the given member padding and pattern,
and returns its id. `PATTERN.CUSTOMIZED` requires `pattern_func`, which upstream
asserts, and every other pattern ignores it. Any value outside `PATTERN` fails an
assert.

parameters.name: is_sticky
parameters.doc:
Whether members are glued to their places in the army, rather than
following them. It shows most while the army rotates.

elements.name: army_members
elements.brief: Returns the ids of the soldiers in an army. The list is the army's own, so editing
elements.description:
Returns the ids of the soldiers in an army. The list is the army's own, so editing
it edits the army.

elements.name: army_remove
elements.brief: Removes an army and releases its members, which stay as soldiers in no army.
elements.description: Removes an army and releases its members, which stay as soldiers in no army.

elements.name: army_update_pattern
elements.brief: Changes an army's pattern and rearranges its members at once. `PATTERN.CUSTOMIZED`
elements.description:
Changes an army's pattern and rearranges its members at once. `PATTERN.CUSTOMIZED`
requires `pattern_func`, which upstream asserts, and every other pattern ignores it.

elements.name: army_update_stickiness
elements.brief: Changes whether an army's members are glued to their places in it.
elements.description: Changes whether an army's members are glued to their places in it.

parameters.name: is_sticky
parameters.doc:
Whether members are glued to their places, rather than following
them.

elements.name: army_debug_draw
elements.brief: Draws an army's center and facing for one frame, by posting `draw_line` to
elements.description:
Draws an army's center and facing for one frame, by posting `draw_line` to
`@render:`. Call it every frame to keep it shown.

elements.name: soldier_create
elements.brief: Creates a soldier and returns its id, joining it to an army when `army_id` is given.
elements.description: Creates a soldier and returns its id, joining it to an army when `army_id` is given.

parameters.name: initial_direction
parameters.doc:
The direction the soldier's game object faces at zero
rotation. Every rotation `soldier_move` returns is relative to it.

elements.name: soldier_join_army
elements.brief: Moves a soldier into an army, out of the army it was in.
elements.description: Moves a soldier into an army, out of the army it was in.

elements.name: soldier_leave_army
elements.brief: Takes a soldier out of its army and rearranges the members left. A soldier in no
elements.description:
Takes a soldier out of its army and rearranges the members left. A soldier in no
army is left as it is. At `v1` the rearrangement raises a Lua error when the soldier
was the army's last member, so call `army_remove` instead in that case.

elements.name: soldier_remove
elements.brief: Removes a soldier completely, rearranging the army it was in. `soldier_move` then
elements.description:
Removes a soldier completely, rearranging the army it was in. `soldier_move` then
returns `undefined` for both values. At `v1` the rearrangement raises a Lua error
when the soldier was the army's last member, so call `army_remove` first in that
case.

elements.name: soldier_debug_on
elements.brief: Turns on a soldier's debug marks: each `soldier_move` call then posts `draw_line` to
elements.description:
Turns on a soldier's debug marks: each `soldier_move` call then posts `draw_line` to
`@render:` to mark the position the soldier is heading for with a cross.

elements.name: soldier_debug_off
elements.brief: Turns off a soldier's debug marks.
elements.description: Turns off a soldier's debug marks.

elements.name: soldier_move
elements.brief: Calculates a soldier's next position and rotation, moving it toward its place in its
elements.description:
Calculates a soldier's next position and rotation, moving it toward its place in its
army. A soldier in no army keeps `current_position`. Returns `undefined` for both
values once the soldier is removed:
`const [position, rotation] = defarmy.soldier_move(id, go.get_position(), speed)`.

parameters.name: speed
parameters.doc: How far the soldier moves this call.

parameters.name: threshold
parameters.doc:
The distance from its place within which the soldier counts as
placed. Defaults to `1`.
